kernel: the Qwen gated full attention kernels: attn_prep (q/k RMSNorm, partial RoPE, KV cache write), the split-KV decode pair attn_decode_partial + attn_decode_reduce, and the attn_prefill1..11 family with the attn11 reduce
summary: Decode attention for the Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 (qwen35.cpp) and qwen4_exp (qwen4_exp.cpp) families is a split-KV flash-decoding pair: one threadgroup per (chunk, kv head), 16-position K/V tiles staged in threadgroup memory behind 2 barriers per tile, one simdgroup per query head, fp32 partials combined by attn_decode_reduce with a sigmoid gate. The same file also holds the prefill family (attn_prefill through the 11 variants, default attn_prefill11r, 32 queries of one query head per 256-thread threadgroup) plus attn_prep and KV helpers, so both classes are covered here and kernel_class records the decode side. The decode pair dispatches unconditionally for every context; the prefill kernels are replaced by tensor-unit qattn_t kernels on M5-class GPUs for the served head configs.

notes: The doc's claim that kapitsa stages 16-position tiles with 2 barriers is confirmed exactly: kTile 16 (attn.metal:84) with barriers at attn.metal:118 and 134. The doc calls this kapitsa's 'decode GQA attention'; the decode pair is indeed the only decode path and dispatches unconditionally (no gate, no single-threadgroup fallback) in enc_attn and the qwen4_exp equivalent, while the same file also holds the whole prefill family plus attn_prep and KV helpers, covered here. Two doc nuances to record: (1) on M5-class GPUs (apple_family >= 10, macOS 26) kapitsa's own prefill no longer runs this file's prefill kernels for the served head configs, because the qattn_t tensor-unit kernels take over (qwen35.cpp:3158, 3165); attn_prefill11r remains the default on M4-class and the fallback elsewhere, and decode attention has no tensor-unit replacement. (2) The decode kernel serves head_dim 256 only (kHD hardcoded) but any G = Hq/Hkv, one simdgroup per query head with sg >= G lanes idling through the barriers; our doc's comparison row ('ours serves head_dim 128 or 256 with at most 8 query heads per KV head') is about our kernel, and kapitsa's constraint is different in both directions. The repo's own measured numbers for these kernels are prefill-side comments (bench_attn); no upstream per-kernel number exists for the decode pair in the source, so the measured block holds only prefill rows. Nemotron and Flint families do not use this file (their own nh_attn.metal and flint.metal). The v1-v10 prefill kernels are reachable only through the NI_ATTN override; the 11 family is what ships.
